facts.fact: 叙述者在仅此一年的大学生活里（二月）待在 SUNY Nowhere，厌恶那种「四面无人、天黑就进屋」的状态；她认为正因离开城市、眼睛得以适应空旷，才有了第一次真正的见鬼（空地让鬼更显眼）。
facts.anchor: It was February in my first and only year of college up in SUNY Nowhere

facts.fact: 她自述成长中只能瞥见鬼的微光；学会放松眼睛、让影像自己浮现（而非伸手去抓），十几岁起开始看见轮廓，要往中景看它们才会从身旁走过。
facts.anchor: When I was a teenager, I started seeing outlines.

more.anchor: I tried relaxing my eyes and letting them appear instead of trying to snatch them up, which was eventually the trick

facts.fact: 写生课上总有同一个女生占她旁边的画架：话多、被老师要求安静；她不断发问（在读什么、为何从不穿彩色、要不要主修艺术、圣诞做了什么），连她那样冷淡也被问出回答；但她总拒绝对方课后午饭的邀约，谎称有课，其实是在图书馆后面抽烟。
facts.anchor: there was this one girl in my figure-drawing class who always took the easel next to mine

more.anchor: But I always said no when she asked me to have lunch after. I told her I had another class, but really I was just smoking behind the library with the other kids who were sure to drop out

facts.fact: 春季学期 Intermediate Figure Drawing：那女生（Mary Ellen）又坐她旁边，寒假过后喜悦全无、心事重重、几乎不动笔，只画了「人的最淡炭色」；下课时叙述者主动约她吃午饭并说「我课表不同」，对方说有课，对另约时间一言不发。
facts.anchor: I asked her to have lunch. My schedule is different, I said, like it was some huge kindness to her. She said she had class, and then said nothing when I suggested meeting some other time.

more.anchor: all her joy seemed to have fled over winter break. She seemed…preoccupied, didn’t make conversation with me or with anyone. When it was time to draw, she barely moved. I kept sneaking a glimpse at her sketch pad—just the barest charcoal shade of a person

facts.fact: 当天晚些时候，Mary Ellen 从图书馆十五楼跳下；课程取消、大家留在宿舍、女生相拥而泣；美术老师为她默哀，除叙述者外所有人都闭眼；她的座位一直空着。
facts.anchor: Later that day, she jumped off the fifteenth floor of the library.

more.anchor: Our art teacher held a moment of silence for her, and everyone but me closed their eyes

facts.fact: 学期稍晚（名义春天但很冷），她参加一场反集会：为对抗天主教学生会的「未出生者」烛光守夜，两侧隔雪地草坪对峙；对方约二十人持长烛不发一言，一男一女举「RIGHT TO LIFE」牌，妇女小组举「MOTHERHOOD BY CHOICE」「FREE US FROM THE CROSS OF RELIGIOUS OPPRESSION」；她去是为了和 Brenda Tornick 挽臂。
facts.anchor: The counterprotest was a response to the Catholic Students Association’s candlelight vigil for the unborn. They didn’t have that much of a turnout—about twenty people stood in the dark with long, lit tapers, not saying a word

more.anchor: I was there to link arms with Brenda
The women’s group, meanwhile, stood on the opposite end of the quad with our own movement signs
The two groups were separated by a wide lawn covered in last week’s snow and thick anticipation

facts.fact: 她看见该女生（Mary Ellen）的鬼魂在集会正中走近：裙摆拖过雪却不湿、不留下脚印；全场只有另一个蓝眼男生也看见——他先低声念、继而喊「你并非真实」，像幼儿般向前扑倒、所有蜡烛一齐熄灭，他脸朝下摔进雪里，甩开搀扶者离开，鬼魂也已消失。
facts.anchor: the hem of her dress trailed in the snow but didn’t get wet, and she left no footprints

more.anchor: like a toddler in anguish, he heaved himself forward, and all their candles went out in a hush
but he landed face down in the snow. Some of the Catholics tried to help him up, but he thrashed away from everyone and stalked off away from the protest

facts.fact: 几天内流言查明：在守夜上失控者是 Mary Ellen 的前男友 Rick Krakus（青梅竹马，据称在开学前把她甩得很狠）；众人断定他疯了，而叙述者断定他所经历的为真、只是他拼命否认；她想跟母亲谈却觉得无处可打这样的电话，且预知母亲会说什么（坏能量/酸空气、排犹遗传、星盘）；她意识到真正吓到她的是目睹他人之痛，遂决定回到一座人们各管各事、却不会对困境者视而不见的城市。
facts.anchor: everyone knew that the guy who had freaked out at the vigil was Mary Ellen’s ex-boyfriend, Rick Krakus

more.anchor: I had to get back to a city that was filled with people who would mind their own business but wouldn’t ignore you if you were in need.

relations.fact: 叙述者 ↔ Mary Ellen Bishop：写生课同学、每次占相邻画架；对方热络搭话，叙述者起初一概拒绝午饭，春季学期才反过来主动约她，却已来不及。
relations.anchor: we had Intermediate Figure Drawing, and she was next to me again

relations.fact: Mary Ellen ↔ Rick Krakus：前男友、青梅竹马；据称开学前把她甩得很狠（也或说他彻底不再理她），她在公共场合想对质却被无视；他在生命权守夜的失控被视为赎罪或崩溃。
relations.anchor: He had been her childhood sweetheart, and he had allegedly dumped her hard right before classes started

relations.fact: 叙述者 ↔ Brenda Tornick：叙述者想追求的对象，Buffalo 来的话多棕发女、口音重、属于妇女小组；她参加反集会是为与其挽臂。
relations.anchor: I had been trying to work up the nerve to make a move on Brenda Tornick, a mouthy brunette from Buffalo

relations.fact: 叙述者 ↔ 母亲：母亲在她幼年就看出她是 queer（因为真正把她当人了解）；十六岁离家搭车去底特律、再去墨西哥城看 Diego Rivera 壁画受的教育；会把这类事说成坏能量/酸空气、排犹遗传、以及星盘，从不明说。
relations.anchor: got her education by leaving home at sixteen and hitchhiking to Detroit and then Mexico City to see Diego Rivera’s murals

more.anchor: she was always saying stuff about being sensitive to bad energy or sour air, way before it was groovy

relations.fact: 叙述者 ↔ Julie：家乡时期的关系人；她不敢在高中与 Julie 牵手，Julie 曾主张她该一起去 City，而母亲要她「吸新鲜空气」。
relations.anchor: I wouldn’t walk around my high school holding hands with Julie

more.anchor: Julie had been right—I should have gone to City with her

relations.fact: 母亲阵营 ↔ Bianca 的母亲 Lupe：叙述者自小在运动妇女中长大（母亲是 red-diaper baby），Lupe 属于在波多黎各组织反对强制绝育的团体。
relations.anchor: Bianca’s mother, Lupe, was part of a group that organized against sterilization abuse in Puerto Rico

relations.fact: 叙述者 ↔ 无名蓝眼男生（后揭示为 Rick）：集会上除她之外唯一看见鬼的人；她认定他的体验是真的，他只是拒绝承认。
relations.anchor: There was one other person who noticed she was there

more.anchor: Whatever he experienced was real, but he was hell-bent on denying it

numbers.anchor: my first and only year of college
I was eighteen and these were my own insecurities
the fifteenth floor of the library
hitchhiking to Detroit and then Mexico City
about twenty people stood in the dark with long, lit tapers
One guy and one girl held a sign
spending Tuesday mornings sketching beside her
the world above Fourteenth Street was narrower
a wide lawn covered in last week’s snow

numbers.anchor: The first day of the spring semester
Within a few days, everyone knew

numbers.fact: Pisces in the eighth house / Scorpio
numbers.anchor: my sun is in Pisces in the eighth house, and you, my darling, have a stellium in Scorpio

turning_point.fact: 转折点：她在反集会上第一次看见完整的鬼——Mary Ellen Bishop 的亡魂；而真正让她恐惧、并促使她离开、回到城市的，不是鬼或自杀的悲伤，而是目睹他人痛苦这种过于私密的经历。
turning_point.anchor: I had just witnessed my first fully formed ghost
